MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  MAY 10, 2016

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 5:30 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

  ***

  At 5:30 p.m., the COUNCIL convened into Closed Session.

  ***

  At 7:02 p.m., the COUNCIL reconvened into open session with MAYOR
  ZUCKERMAN, MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, COUNCILWOMAN HUFF,
  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL and COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ present.

  ***
14.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  DISCUSSION WITH RESPECT TO PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT: QUARTERLY CITY
  MANAGER REVIEW
  (Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957)

  NO ACTION WAS TAKEN.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Direct Andy Clark
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

Others Present:  Pam Schachter, Park and Activities Commission
  Tim Scott, Planning Commission

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION

  A PROCLAMATION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES PROCLAIMING THE MONTH OF MAY AS "MATERNAL MENTAL
  HEALTH AWARENESS MONTH"

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted her pleasure at presenting Drs. Berkowitz
  and Handler with a Proclamation. She shared her experience with postpartum
  depression, and because of their support, she was able to overcome this
  condition.

  Dr. Handler commented that recognition of this mood disorder helps to de-
  stigmatize and manage this illness.

  Dr. Berkowitz further commented that this affects the entire family and is
  thankful for the City’s acknowledgement. She then announced an upcoming
  Harbor-UCLA Community Awareness Forum.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
MAY 10, 2016
 B.  WASTE MANAGEMENT DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR'S FREE RESIDENTIAL
  REFUSE SERVICE

  Janine Hamner, Community Affairs, Waste Management, presented the
  COUNCIL with two checks for the “At Your Door” service that accepts
  Household Hazardous Waste. She explained how this program works at no
  charge to the resident.

  Ms. Hamner drew the name of Leon Zukinski, Rollingwood Drive, as the
  recipient of one year's free disposal service.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 26, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL requested a correction under Item 9A - NEW
  BUSINESS, Paragraph 3:

  “COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL further noted that the Chamber suggested having a
  “restaurant week” in July is planning a “Dine Around the Peninsula
  Restaurant Week” on July 15-24 for those businesses who are members of the
  Chamber.”

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 12, 2016 AS
  AMENDED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – APRIL AND MAY

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 56760 THROUGH 56807 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $107,831.89; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040116 THROUGH 040216;
  56624 THROUGH 56636; 56684 THROUGH 56700; 56742 THROUGH
  56747 IN THE AMOUNT OF $213,018.67 FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $320,850.56 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)\

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A AND B.

A.  BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS FY 2015-16

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Budget Amendments for
  Fiscal Year 2015-16.

  APPROVED THE BUDGET AMENDMENTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2015-16.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 10, 2016
 B.  YOUTH EMPLOYMENT PLAN FOR LOS ANGELES COUNTY 1996 SAFE
  NEIGHBORHOOD PARKS PROPOSITION "A" SPECIFIED GRANT FOR THE
  DEVELOPMENT OF EQUESTRIAN FACILITIES PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt the Youth Employment Plan to
  comply with the Los Angeles County 1996 Safe Neighborhood Park Proposition
  "A" Specified Grant Fund requirements for the Development of Equestrian
  Facilities Project.

  ADOPTED THE YOUTH EMPLOYMENT PLAN.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

A.  FRANCISCO  MARTINEZ,  GOVERNMENT  AFFAIRS  REPRESENTATIVE,
  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON

  Francisco Martinez updated the COUNCIL on the STIRRUP Project that will
  replace the poles, transformers, etc., on Carriage Drive, Gaucho Drive, Estribo
  Drive, and Potrillo Road.

  Mr. Martinez then referred to the Rule 20A Project that will remove the poles on
  Palos Verdes Drive North/Palos Verdes Drive East. He noted that he has met with
  Assistant City Manager Grammer to identify the utilities (AT & T Mobility and
  Crown Castle) still remaining on the poles. He further noted that they are
  scheduled to come down in the next few weeks.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that the City receives bulletins from SCE announcing
  streets that will be without power temporarily and asked if specific addresses
  could be provided. Mr. Martinez responded that they only list rough boundaries
  due to the homeowners’ privacy and security.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  AUTHORIZATION TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR RESURFACING PROJECT ON
  VARIOUS CITY STREETS AND MULTI-USE PEDESTRIAN PATHS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the specifications and bid
  documents and authorize the solicitation of bids for the 2016 Resurfacing
  Project on Various Streets and Multi-Use Pedestrian Paths Project.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  noted that the parking lot at Highridge Park is included and the tree roots will
  undergo pruning where necessary.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  noted that this project is set to begin in July when school is not in session.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL referred to the depletion of Quimby funds and
  asked if any other park improvements are slated.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  noted that additional Quimby funds would be received in phases from the
  Chandler development. He further noted that funds will also be collected from
  the former car wash project as well as 927 Deep Valley Drive over the next two
  to four years.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 10, 2016
   MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN also pointed out that there are separate
  equestrian funds available. City Manager Prichard stated that those equestrian
  funds are more restrictive in that they are coming from the designated Chandler
  special equestrian donation. Finally he noted that the City is still waiting on a
  grant reimbursement for the Peter Weber Equestrian Center Project and that
  any shortfall will be made up from those special equestrian donation funds.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE SPECIFICATIONS AND BID DOCUMENTS AND
  AUTHORIZE THE SOLICITATION OF BIDS FOR THE 2016
  RESURFACING PROJECT ON VARIOUS STREETS AND MULTI-USE
  PEDESTRIAN PATHS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

B.  WASTE MANAGEMENT CONTRACT REVIEW

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Direct staff to negotiate a new
  contract with Waste Management for continued collection services for
  residential and commercial solid waste, recyclable materials, manure and green
  waste for final approval by the City Council; 2) Inform Waste Management by
  written notice of the City's intent to negotiate a new contract and setting the
  terms for negotiation; and 3)  Appoint a City Council subcommittee to
  participate in the negotiation process.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  Richard Tagore-Irwin, R3 Consulting Group, provided an extensive presentation
  of Waste Management’s contract review that included a billing audit/field audit,
  possible amendments to their agreement, monitoring, diversion issues,
  methodology for tracking origin, vehicle specifications, including weight and
  noise testing, carts/bins, call center, co-mingling of refuse with other cities,
  rates and franchise fees. He noted that overall, they have performed favorably,
  but there are a few items that need to be addressed.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Tagore-Irwin noted that an organics
  program must be implemented and acknowledged that there are not enough
  composting facilities in the area.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, Mr. Tagore-Irwin noted that, if an
  extension is desirable, the term should be seven to ten years in order to allow
  the franchisee to amortize capital investment.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that the last negotiated contract was a
  rigorous process and that he and former Council Member Addleman took a
  significant amount of time to educate themselves. He commended Mr. Tagore-
  Irwin on his excellent work as well as Waste Management on their performance
  for the City.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted his surprise at the decrease in the City’s
  AB 939 diversion rate. He further noted that he is in favor of negotiating with
  Waste Management, along with Mr. Tagore-Irwin’s assistance, to address those
  issues raised.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted her appreciation for MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN providing context of the prior contract negotiations.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 10, 2016
   MAYOR PRO  TEM  ZERUNYAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCILWOMAN
  MITCHELL

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO: 1) NEGOTIATE A NEW CONTRACT WITH WASTE
  MANAGEMENT FOR CONTINUED COLLECTION SERVICES FOR
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL SOLID WASTE, RECYCLABLE
  MATERIALS, MANURE AND GREEN WASTE FOR FINAL APPROVAL BY
  THE CITY COUNCIL 2) INFORM WASTE MANAGEMENT BY WRITTEN
  NOTICE OF THE CITY’S INTENT TO NEGOTIATE A NEW CONTRACT AND
  SETTING THE TERMS FOR NEGOTIATION; AND 3) APPOINT MAYOR PRO
  TEM ZERUNYAN AND COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ TO A SUBCOMMITTEE
  TO PARTICIPATE IN THE NEGOTIATION PROCESS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH INTERIOR ARCHITECTS FOR
  CITY HALL AND CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS REDESIGN PROJECT
  PREPARATION AND MANAGEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Professional Services
  Agreement with Interior Architects to proceed with the City Hall and City
  Council Chambers redesign project preparation and management in an amount
  not to exceed $74,888.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per
  agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead noted that the proposed conference room should not affect the
  natural light in the front office, but that this will be addressed.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted his concern regarding the requested amount and
  potential add-on costs for lighting and signage. Assistant to the City Manager
  Davis noted that those items were not part of the initial scope.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN concurred with MAYOR ZUCKERMAN regarding
  his concerns about the overall cost and the lighting and signage line items.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that it appears there is a conflict between
  the proposal and the contract with regards to several items including the
  lighting. She referred to additional design services that may be needed, and it
  was her preference to avoid any change orders.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  INTERIOR ARCHITECTS FOR THE CITY HALL AND CITY COUNCIL
  CHAMBERS REDESIGN PROJECT PREPARATION AND MANAGEMENT
  TO INCLUDE THE LIGHTING DESIGN.

  Discussion continued where MAYOR ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by
  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO AMEND THE PREVIOUS MOTION TO APPROVE THE PROFESSIONAL
  SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH INTERIOR ARCHITECTS FOR THE CITY
  HALL AND CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS REDESIGN PROJECT
  PREPARATION AND MANAGEMENT TO INCLUDE THE LIGHTING AND
  SIGNAGE DESIGNS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MAY 10, 2016
 B.  AWARD OF BID - SLURRY SEAL PROJECT ON VARIOUS CITY STREETS

  Recommendation: That the City Council award the bid in the amount of
  $222,195 to All American Asphalt for the FY 2015-16 Slurry Seal Project on
  Various City Streets.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Assistant City Manager Grammer noted
  that residents will be advised to shut off their sprinklers when this work takes
  place.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO AWARD THE BID IN THE AMOUNT OF $222,195 TO ALL AMERICAN
  ASPHALT FOR THE FY 2015-16 SLURRY SEAL PROJECT ON VARIOUS
  CITY STREETS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  In response to City Manager Prichard, Assistant City Manager Grammer was
  pleased to note that the City is on schedule to complete all of the recommended
  projects of the 2014 Pavement Management System analysis.

C.  STREET TREE MAINTENANCE SERVICES ANALYSIS

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to solicit bids for street tree
  maintenance services.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  Victor Gonzales, Vice President, West Coast Arborists, noted that they have
  enjoyed their relationship with the City. He further noted that he recognizes the
  need for the City to solicit bids and would be happy to submit a proposal.

  Additionally, he explained the State’s interpretation of workers’ classifications and
  the resulting need to enter into a new wage rate agreement which resulted in
  substantial labor cost increases.

  City Manager Prichard noted that Mr. Gonzales’ explanation was correct and that
  this concern was brought to the City a year ago. He further noted that, given the
  City’s responsibilities for ensuring the wise expenditure of public dollars, it would
  be a good time to go out to bid and thanked Mr. Gonzales for his comments.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR STREET TREE MAINTENANCE
  SERVICES.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  NONE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MAY 10, 2016
 12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF APRIL 19, 2016 -
  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF referred to the discussion regarding electric vehicle
  charging stations and reiterated that staff will further assess locations in the
  commercial district.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  MINUTES OF APRIL 9, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that the City has an ordinance requiring
  residents to install a charging station for new development.

  Tim Scott, Planning Commissioner, also noted that private vendors install
  charging stations and through their business model are able to generate a profit
  at no cost to the City or developers.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF then referred to the coyote discussion and that perhaps
  the City could post an article on the website. COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted
  that information is already provided on the website and the County also keeps a
  record of how many incidents occur.

B.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF APRIL 25, 2016 - COUNCILWOMAN
  SCHMITZ

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF
  APRIL 25, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or

  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

  NONE

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 9:08 p.m. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN formally adjourned the City Council

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
